title: Part Eleven: Taxes, Fees and the Benefits Cliff

sections.brief: Who pays across all taxes: CBO 2023/2022 federal rates by quintile (1.4%/23.2%/31.5%, top fifth 70% of taxes, income tax -11% bottom) and 1979-2007 series; ITEP Who Pays 7th ed. state/local (11.3% bottom vs 7.2% top 1%) and ITEP 2024 combined (17.1% to 34.8%, 'just barely progressive'); payroll tax and $184,500 cap arithmetic; wages vs long-term gains (37% vs 23.8%); Saez-Zucman 23% vs 24.2% and 2025 24% vs 30%, against TPC, Splinter (38%/25%) and Cato (contested); CBO on P.L. 119-21 (lowest decile -$1,200, top +$13,600; status Oct 2026). Figures: stats; compare (wages vs gains); compare (told vs record)

Drip pricing and the FTC fees rule (17 Dec 2024, 4-1; effective 12 May 2025; tickets and short-term lodging; 53m hours/$11bn time value; $10m StubHub settlement 9 Apr 2026); EIA 2024 utility shutoffs 15.1m, 122m notices, 12.6m reconnections; Ferguson DOJ 2015 (fines 12% to 23% of general revenue, 9,000+ warrants, revenue emails); Governing 2019 (~600 jurisdictions >10%, median big city 2%); debt-based licence suspensions (11m, 25 states + DC reforms, 42 cents per dollar); bank fees left to Part Nine. Figures: flow; money; stats

Clinton 1993 'work pays' promise; EMTR defined; plateau vs cliff (Atlanta Fed); stacking arithmetic for a single parent of two (payroll 7.65 + EITC 21.06 + SNAP up to 30); CCDF 85% SMI cliff and ASPE 2019 EMTRs (67/73/79%, 37% lose subsidy); 7% copay cap repealed 2026; Medicaid 138%; ACA 400% cliff returned 2026 (WV couple $500 more income -> $43,776 cheapest plan); SSI $2,000; Atlanta Fed CLIFF 'Leia' example (-$11,000, -$35,000, positive lifetime); counter-evidence CBO 31% average, ASPE 10% cliff vs 15% negative, EITC phase-in 40%, Kleven 2024 reappraisal; 2025-26 SNAP and Medicaid work rules; labelled Interpretation passage with counter-readings. Figures: flow; money
